notes.note: Huawei estimated shipments for the Ascend AI chip series were approximately 700,000 units in 2025. While 2026 projections reach 1.6 million silicon dies, this figure includes inventory and yield loss rather than millions of finished chips shipped. https://technode.com/2025/05/18/huawei-to-ship-700000-ascend-ai-chips-in-2025-despite-yield-challenges/ https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-09-29/huawei-to-double-output-of-top-ai-chip-as-nvidia-wavers-in-china

notes.opus_reason: The words are Jensen Huang's, not Dwarkesh's, and Dwarkesh is pushing back throughout this passage, so a note here corrects the guest rather than the host. The number matters to the episode's central argument, because Jensen uses it to say China can already make enough chips without Nvidia, so the correction is not pedantic. Every public estimate I can find is well under a million Ascend accelerators: Mizuho's forecast was about 700,000 units for 2025, a US Commerce official told Congress in June 2025 the figure was no more than 200,000, and Huawei's 2026 plan of roughly 600,000 Ascend 910C units was reported as about double the 2025 output, with up to 1.6 million dies across the whole Ascend line. What gives me pause is that Jensen said 'chips' in a throwaway answer, and Huawei ships many more chips than datacenter accelerators, including the cheaper Ascend 310 edge parts and its phone processors, so he could defend 'millions' by pointing at a wider count. The note also carries no verified sources in the pipeline output, and the 700,000 number it leans on is a mid-2025 forecast rather than a measured 2025 result.
